title: egress path MTU and TLS handshake notes
content:
Overview:
Observed intermittent TLS handshake stalls (client side stalls during ClientHello / early handshake) from Private deployment pods when calling external vendor APIs over HTTPS. Issue reproduces more often for endpoints that advertise HTTP/2 (ALPN: h2) and when payloads are larger (e.g., ClientHello+SNI+alpn+ocsp stapling requests). Suspect PMTU / MSS clamping + NAT/peering path fragmentation problem rather than app-layer TLS config.

Environment and topology (short):
- Private deployment in customer VPC A (AWS), private control plane in VPC B.
- VPC A peered to VPC B via VPC Peering (no TGW currently for this customer) for control plane egress.
- Egress to internet goes through a NAT gateway in VPC B (shared egress), then to IGW.
- Observed from inside pod (container image: redwood/deploy-agent:2025-10) using host networking disabled (CNI: aws-vpc-cni).
- MTU on pod's eth0: 1460 (calculated), ENI reports 9001 on the instance (jumbo enabled), but packets observed leaving NAT with DF set sometimes.

Commands run (collected):
- ip link show
  ip link show dev eth0
- ip route get 8.8.8.8
  ip route get <vendor-ip>
- sysctl -a | egrep 'tcp_mtu_probing|clamp_mss|rp_filter'
  sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing -> 0 (before change)
- curl -v --http2 --resolve vendor.test:443:<vendor-ip> "https://vendor.test/health"
  (result: hangs after 'TLS handshake, ClientHello sent', then curl times out)
- openssl s_client -connect <vendor-ip>:443 -servername vendor.test -alpn h2 -msg -debug
  (result: TCP connection established, then no ServerHello, client retransmits ClientHello several times)
- tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap tcp and host <vendor-ip>
  (capture shows ClientHello sent (length ~1800 bytes), followed by retransmissions and then no ServerHello)
- tracepath <vendor-ip>
  (shows first hop MTU 1500 then drops to 1400 at some peering segment)
- mtr -rwzbc 200 <vendor-ip>
  (shows occasional increased latency at NAT gateway and one hop dropping packets ~0.6%)
- iptables -t mangle -L -n -v
  (no explicit clamp_mss rules found)

Observed snippets from tcpdump (annotated):
- 10:12:05.123456 IP pod-10.x.x.x.54321 > vendor.ip.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 29200, options [mss 1360,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
- 10:12:05.123589 IP pod-10.x.x.x.54321 > vendor.ip.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1801, ack 1, win 229, length 1800  # ClientHello large (contains multiple ALPNs + SNI)
- 10:12:05.200123 IP pod-10.x.x.x.54321 > vendor.ip.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1801, ack 1, win 229, length 1800  # retransmit
- 10:12:05.456789 IP our-nat-ip.54321 > vendor.ip.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1801, ack 1, win 229, length 1800  # packet leaves with DF set and never fragmented; likely dropped mid-path

Hypothesis summary (ranked):
1) Path MTU / MSS blackhole: ClientHello is > path MTU on a segment after NAT or peering hop; DF bit prevents fragmentation; intermediate device drops or silently drops fragments leading to retransmits and stalled TLS handshake. Explains why smaller ClientHello (older ciphers or no ALPN) succeed.
2) NAT gateway / firewall appliance is mishandling TCP MSS or incorrectly setting DF on forwarded packets when doing address translation across peering.
3) ALPN / SNI size pushes ClientHello over threshold; server not responding because it never receives full ClientHello.
4) Rarely, TLS stack incompatibility: but server logs (vendor) show no incoming connection attempts for failed cases, supporting network-level loss.

Quick mitigation attempts (what we tried and results):
- Enabled net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on host (sysctl) then restarted container agent: partial improvement, some requests succeed.
- iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on NAT host (temporary): immediate improvement for tested endpoints.
- Forced curl to prefer smaller ciphers / disable h2 (curl --http1.1 --ciphers 'DEFAULT:!ECDHE' ): succeeded consistently (smaller ClientHello).
- Tried iptables MASQUERADE -> SNAT with explicit MTU rewriting on host (tc qdisc) but more invasive.

What vendor said (quick):
- Vendor confirmed they saw no ServerHello attempts correlated to failed client traces. They recommended checking intermediate NAT/firewall MTU and whether DF bit present.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) From affected pod: curl --http2 -v https://vendor.test/health (with resolve to vendor IP) -> observe hang
2) tcpdump before executing: tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/p.pcap host <vendor-ip> and capture while reproducing
3) From jump host in same VPC: tracepath <vendor-ip> and ip route get <vendor-ip>
4) On NAT host: iptables -t mangle -L -n -v and tc -s qdisc show dev eth0

Next steps and todo: (short checklist)
- [ ] Make clamp_mss permanent in NAT host AMI or add as init task for NAT instance (coordinate with infra).
- [ ] Add tcp_mtu_probing=1 as stopgap in deployed nodes until we can pin root cause. Watch for side effects.
- [ ] Run controlled experiment: reproduce with DF toggling (ip route change) and record pcap across each hop.
- [ ] Validate across multiple customers: are only peered-->nat flows affected or also TGW setups?
- [ ] Contact AWS support if we see drops inside AWS-managed NAT (NAT gateway behavior) — include packet captures and tracepath output.
- [ ] Add end-to-end test to private-deploy e2e suite that checks TLS handshake with large ClientHello (ALPN+h2) across peered topology.

Notes / random findings: 
- Instances with ENIs configured for jumbo frames (9001) downstream might still present smaller MTU to containers (CNI / VPC CNI path). Need consistency check between ENI, host, and CNI assigned MTU.
- Some customer firewall appliances (third-party) were found to strip DF or to drop fragments; check vendor appliance logs if present.

Raw commands to re-run quickly: 
- sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
- iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- curl -v --http2 --resolve vendor.test:443:<vendor-ip> https://vendor.test/health
- openssl s_client -connect <vendor-ip>:443 -servername vendor.test -alpn h2 -msg -debug

Capture naming convention for uploads: "pd-<customer>-egress-<date>-<hop>-p.pcap"

Owner and follow-up: Maya Chen (ping @ravi / @sofia for infra changes).

If this is recurring across multiple customers we should consider:
- Baking MSS clamp into our egress-managed NAT AMI and document tradeoffs
- Adding automated detection: if ClientHello retransmits > N times within X seconds, flag as PMTU candidate and automatically enable tcp_mtu_probing on host & notify infra

End of notes.
